sdlc_rationale: Scope definition for what constitutes an 'application' in ASVS is framework documentation
reference: Components that serve, modify, or validate HTTP traffic, such as Web Application Firewalls (WAFs), load balancers, or proxies, may be considered part of the application for those specific purposes.

sdlc_rationale: Scope clarification about components for ASVS requirements is framework documentation.
policy_description: These components should be considered for requirements related to cached responses, rate limiting, or restricting incoming and outgoing connections based on source and destination.

sdlc_rationale: ASVS verifiability requirement definition is framework metadata.
policy_description: The requirement must be verifiable, and the verification must result in a fail or pass decision.

sdlc_rationale: ASVS contains only must requirements is framework metadata.
policy_description: The ASVS only contains requirements (must) and does not contain recommendations (should) as the main condition.

sdlc_rationale: Documentation requirement conventions in ASVS chapters is framework metadata.
policy_description: Documentation requirements are always in the first section of a chapter and always have a related implementation requirement where the decisions that are documented should actually be put into place.

sdlc_rationale: ASVS requirement identifier format description is framework metadata.
policy_description: Each requirement has an identifier in the format <chapter>.<section>.<requirement>, where each element is a number.

sdlc_rationale: ASVS versioning identifier convention is framework metadata.
policy_description: The v preceding the version number in the format should always be lowercase.

sdlc_rationale: ASVS reference version assumption is framework metadata.
policy_description: If identifiers are used without including the v<version> element then they should be assumed to refer to the latest Application Security Verification Standard content.

sdlc_rationale: ASVS verification sufficiency definition (automated tools alone insufficient) is testing guidance metadata.
policy_description: Merely running an automated tool without thorough testing is insufficient for certification, as each requirement must be verifiably tested.

sdlc_rationale: ASVS recommendation for hybrid penetration testing is testing methodology guidance
reference: It is strongly encouraged to perform documentation or source code-led (hybrid) penetration testing, which have full access to the application developers and the application's documentation, rather than traditional penetration tests.

sdlc_rationale: ASVS stance on certification and assurance services is administrative/organizational guidance.
policy_description: Organizations may offer assurance services, provided they do not claim official OWASP certification.

sdlc_rationale: Input decoding/unescaping to canonical form only once before processing is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.1.1 Verify that input is decoded or unescaped into a canonical form only once, it is only decoded when encoded data in that form is expected, and that this is done before processing the input further.

sdlc_rationale: Output encoding as a final step before interpreter use is an implementation-level coding practice.
policy_description: 1.1.2 Verify that the application performs output encoding and escaping either as a final step before being used by the interpreter for which it is intended or by the interpreter itself.

sdlc_rationale: Context-relevant output encoding for HTTP/HTML/XML responses is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.2.1 Verify that output encoding for an HTTP response, HTML document, or XML document is relevant for the context required, to avoid changing the message or document structure.

sdlc_rationale: URL encoding/encoding untrusted data in URLs is an implementation-level coding practice.
policy_description: 1.2.2 Verify that when dynamically building URLs, untrusted data is encoded according to its context and that only safe URL protocols are permitted.

sdlc_rationale: Output encoding when building JavaScript/JSON content is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.2.3 Verify that output encoding or escaping is used when dynamically building JavaScript content (including JSON), to avoid JavaScript and JSON injection.

sdlc_rationale: Using parameterized queries/ORMs for database queries is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.2.4 Verify that data selection or database queries use parameterized queries, ORMs, entity frameworks, or are otherwise protected from SQL Injection and other database injection attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Protecting against OS command injection through parameterized queries or output encoding is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 1.2.5 Verify that the application protects against OS command injection and that operating system calls use parameterized OS queries or use contextual command line output encoding.

sdlc_rationale: LDAP injection prevention is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.2.6 Verify that the application protects against LDAP injection vulnerabilities, or that specific security controls to prevent LDAP injection have been implemented.

sdlc_rationale: XPath injection prevention through query parameterization is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.2.7 Verify that the application is protected against XPath injection attacks by using query parameterization or precompiled queries.

sdlc_rationale: Configuring LaTeX processors securely with allowlisted commands is an implementation-level requirement.
policy_description: 1.2.8 Verify that LaTeX processors are configured securely and an allowlist of commands is used to prevent LaTeX injection attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Escaping special characters in regular expressions is an implementation-level coding practice.
policy_description: 1.2.9 Verify that the application escapes special characters in regular expressions to prevent them from being misinterpreted as metacharacters.

sdlc_rationale: CSV and formula injection prevention through proper escaping is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.2.10 Verify that the application is protected against CSV and Formula Injection by following RFC4180 escaping rules.

sdlc_rationale: Sanitizing untrusted HTML input from WYSIWYG editors using secure libraries is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 1.3.1 Verify that all untrusted HTML input from WYSIWYG editors or similar is sanitized using a well-known and secure HTML sanitization library or framework feature.

sdlc_rationale: Avoiding eval() and dynamic code execution is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.3.2 Verify that the application avoids the use of eval() or other dynamic code execution features. Where there is no alternative, any user input being included must be sanitized before being executed.

sdlc_rationale: Sanitizing data passed to potentially dangerous contexts is an implementation-level coding practice.
policy_description: 1.3.3 Verify that data being passed to a potentially dangerous context is sanitized beforehand to enforce safety measures.

sdlc_rationale: Validating/sanitizing user-supplied SVG content is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.3.4 Verify that user-supplied SVG scriptable content is validated or sanitized to contain only safe tags and attributes.

sdlc_rationale: Sanitizing or disabling user-supplied scriptable template language content is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 1.3.5 Verify that the application sanitizes or disables user-supplied scriptable or expression template language content.

sdlc_rationale: SSRF protection through allowlist validation of protocols
policy_description: paths
reference: and ports is an implementation practice.
column11: 1.3.6 Verify that the application protects against SSRF attacks, by validating untrusted data against an allowlist of protocols, domains, paths and ports.

sdlc_rationale: Template injection protection by not building templates from untrusted input is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 1.3.7 Verify that the application protects against template injection attacks by not allowing templates to be built based on untrusted input.

sdlc_rationale: Sanitizing untrusted input in JNDI queries and configuring JNDI securely is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 1.3.8 Verify that the application appropriately sanitizes untrusted input before use in JNDI queries and that JNDI is configured securely to prevent JNDI injection attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Sanitizing content before sending to memcache is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.3.9 Verify that the application sanitizes content before it is sent to memcache to prevent injection attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Sanitizing format strings before processing is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.3.10 Verify that format strings which might resolve in an unexpected or malicious way when used are sanitized before being processed.

sdlc_rationale: Sanitizing user input before passing to mail systems to prevent SMTP/IMAP injection is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 1.3.11 Verify that the application sanitizes user input before passing to mail systems to protect against SMTP or IMAP injection.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring regular expressions are free from exponential backtracking and sanitizing untrusted input for ReDoS prevention is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 1.3.12 Verify that regular expressions are free from elements causing exponential backtracking, and ensure untrusted input is sanitized to mitigate ReDoS or Runaway Regex attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Using memory-safe string handling and pointer arithmetic to prevent buffer/heap overflows is an implementation-level practice.
policy_description: 1.4.1 Verify that the application uses memory-safe string, safer memory copy and pointer arithmetic to detect or prevent stack, buffer, or heap overflows.
reference: 1.4.1; V1.4 Memory, String, and Unmanaged Code

sdlc_rationale: Using sign
policy_description: and input validation to prevent integer overflows is an implementation-level practice.
column10: 1.4.2 Verify that sign, range, and input validation techniques are used to prevent integer overflows.
column11: 1.4.2; V1.4 Memory, String, and Unmanaged Code

sdlc_rationale: Releasing dynamically allocated memory and removing freed pointers is an implementation-level coding practice.
policy_description: 1.4.3 Verify that dynamically allocated memory and resources are released, and that references or pointers to freed memory are removed or set to null to prevent dangling pointers and use-after-free vulnerabilities.
reference: 1.4.3; V1.4 Memory, String, and Unmanaged Code

sdlc_rationale: Configuring XML parsers to use restrictive settings and disable external entity resolution is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 1.5.1 Verify that the application configures XML parsers to use a restrictive configuration and that unsafe features such as resolving external entities are disabled to prevent XXE attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing safe input handling for deserialization of untrusted data is an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 1.5.2 Verify that deserialization of untrusted data enforces safe input handling, such as using an allowlist of object types or restricting client-defined object types, to prevent deserialization attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Using consistent parsers and character encoding for the same data type is an implementation-level practice.
policy_description: 1.5.3 Verify that different parsers used in the application for the same data type perform parsing in a consistent way and use the same character encoding mechanism.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting input validation rules in application documentation is primarily a design/requirements activity.
policy_description: 2.1.1 Verify that the application's documentation defines input validation rules for how to check the validity of data items against an expected structure.
reference: 2.1.1; V2.1 Validation and Business Logic Documentation

sdlc_rationale: Documenting combined data item consistency validation is primarily a design/requirements activity.
policy_description: 2.1.2 Verify that the application's documentation defines how to validate the logical and contextual consistency of combined data items.
reference: 2.1.2; V2.1 Validation and Business Logic Documentation

sdlc_rationale: Documenting business logic limits and validations is a design/requirements documentation activity.
policy_description: 2.1.3 Verify that expectations for business logic limits and validations are documented, including both per-user and globally across the application.
reference: 2.1.3; V2.1 Validation and Business Logic Documentation

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing business/functional expectations through input validation is an implementation-level coding practice.
policy_description: 2.2.1 Verify that input is validated to enforce business or functional expectations for that input.

sdlc_rationale: Designing input validation to be enforced at a trusted service layer is primarily a design principle.
policy_description: 2.2.2 Verify that the application is designed to enforce input validation at a trusted service layer.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring combinations of related data items are reasonable per pre-defined rules is an implementation-level practice.
policy_description: 2.2.3 Verify that the application ensures that combinations of related data items are reasonable according to the pre-defined rules.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing sequential business logic flow processing without step skipping is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 2.3.1 Verify that the application will only process business logic flows for the same user in the expected sequential step order and without skipping steps.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing business logic limits per documentation to avoid exploitation is an implementation-level requirement.
policy_description: 2.3.2 Verify that business logic limits are implemented per the application's documentation to avoid business logic flaws being exploited.

sdlc_rationale: Using transactions for business logic operations to ensure atomicity is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 2.3.3 Verify that transactions are being used at the business logic level such that either a business logic operation succeeds in its entirety or it is rolled back to the previous correct state.

sdlc_rationale: Using business logic locking mechanisms to prevent double-booking of limited resources is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 2.3.4 Verify that business logic level locking mechanisms are used to ensure that limited quantity resources cannot be double-booked by manipulating the application's logic.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring multi-user approval for high-value business logic flows is an implementation requirement.
policy_description: 2.3.5 Verify that high-value business logic flows require multi-user approval to prevent unauthorized or accidental actions.

sdlc_rationale: Anti-automation controls to protect against excessive calls are an implementation-level coding requirement.
policy_description: 2.4.1 Verify that anti-automation controls are in place to protect against excessive calls to application functions.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring realistic human timing to prevent excessively rapid transaction submissions is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 2.4.2 Verify that business logic flows require realistic human timing, preventing excessively rapid transaction submissions.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting expected security features browsers must support is a design/requirements documentation activity.
policy_description: 3.1.1 Verify that application documentation states the expected security features that browsers using the application must support.

sdlc_rationale: Preventing browsers from rendering content in incorrect contexts is an implementation-level security header practice.
policy_description: 3.2.1 Verify that security controls are in place to prevent browsers from rendering content or functionality in HTTP responses in an incorrect context.

sdlc_rationale: Using safe rendering functions for text content to prevent unintended HTML/JS execution is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.2.2 Verify that content intended to be displayed as text is handled using safe rendering functions to prevent unintended execution.

sdlc_rationale: Avoiding DOM clobbering through explicit declarations and strict type checking is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.2.3 Verify that the application avoids DOM clobbering when using client-side JavaScript.

sdlc_rationale: Setting cookie Secure attribute and using Secure/Host prefixes is an implementation-level cookie security practice.
policy_description: 3.3.1 Verify that cookies have the Secure attribute set, and the appropriate prefix is used for the cookie name.

sdlc_rationale: Setting SameSite cookie attribute to prevent CSRF and UI redress attacks is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.3.2 Verify that each cookie's SameSite attribute value is set according to the purpose of the cookie.

sdlc_rationale: Using __Host- prefix for cookies not designed for sharing with other hosts is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.3.3 Verify that cookies have the __Host- prefix for the cookie name unless they are explicitly designed to be shared with other hosts.

sdlc_rationale: Setting HttpOnly attribute for cookies that should not be accessible to client-side scripts is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.3.4 Verify that if the value of a cookie is not meant to be accessible to client-side scripts, the cookie must have the HttpOnly attribute set.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing cookie size limits to ensure cookies are stored and sent by browsers is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.3.5 Verify that when the application writes a cookie the cookie name and value length combined are not over 4096 bytes.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing HSTS headers with minimum age is an implementation practice for HTTP security.
policy_description: 3.4.1 Verify that a Strict-Transport-Security header field is included on all responses. A maximum age of at least 1 year must be defined.
reference: 3.4.1; V3.4 Browser Security Mechanism Headers; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing CORS with allowlist validation is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 3.4.2 Verify that the CORS Access-Control-Allow-Origin header field is a fixed value or validated against an allowlist of trusted origins.
reference: 3.4.2; V3.4 Browser Security Mechanism Headers; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Setting Content-Security-Policy headers to restrict trusted content is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.4.3 Verify that HTTP responses include a Content-Security-Policy header field which defines directives to ensure the browser only loads and executes trusted content or resources.
reference: 3.4.3; V3.4 Browser Security Mechanism Headers; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Setting X-Content-Type-Options to prevent MIME sniffing is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 3.4.4 Verify that all HTTP responses contain an X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff header field.
reference: 3.4.4; V3.4 Browser Security Mechanism Headers; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Setting Referrer-Policy to prevent data leakage via Referer header is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.4.5 Verify that the application sets a referrer policy to prevent leakage of sensitive data via the Referer HTTP request header field.
reference: 3.4.5; V3.4 Browser Security Mechanism Headers; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Using CSP frame-ancestors directive to prevent clickjacking is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.4.6 Verify that the web application uses the frame-ancestors directive of CSP for every HTTP response to ensure it cannot be embedded by default.
reference: 3.4.6; V3.4 Browser Security Mechanism Headers; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Configuring CSP to report violations is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.4.7 Verify that the Content-Security-Policy header field specifies a location to report violations.
reference: 3.4.7; V3.4 Browser Security Mechanism Headers; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Setting Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy headers to prevent window object sharing attacks is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.4.8 Verify that all HTTP responses that initiate a document rendering include the Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header field with the same-origin directive.
reference: 3.4.8; V3.4 Browser Security Mechanism Headers; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Validating requests originate from the application to prevent CSRF is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.5.1 Verify that if the application does not rely on CORS preflight to prevent disallowed cross-origin requests these requests are validated to ensure they originate from the application itself.
reference: 3.5.1; V3.5 Browser Origin Separation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Verifying CORS preflight is not bypassable for sensitive functionality is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.5.2 Verify that if the application relies on CORS preflight it is not possible to call the functionality with a request which does not trigger a CORS-preflight request.
reference: 3.5.2; V3.5 Browser Origin Separation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Restricting HTTP methods for sensitive functionality is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.5.3 Verify that HTTP requests to sensitive functionality use appropriate HTTP methods such as POST PUT PATCH or DELETE.
reference: 3.5.3; V3.5 Browser Origin Separation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Hosting separate applications on different host names to leverage same-origin policy is a design-level architectural decision.
policy_description: 3.5.4 Verify that separate applications are hosted on different host names to leverage the restrictions provided by same-origin policy.
reference: 3.5.4; V3.5 Browser Origin Separation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Validating origin of postMessage messages is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 3.5.5 Verify that messages received by the postMessage interface are discarded if the origin is not trusted.
reference: 3.5.5; V3.5 Browser Origin Separation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Disabling JSONP to prevent XSSI attacks is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 3.5.6 Verify that JSONP functionality is not enabled anywhere across the application to avoid Cross-Site Script Inclusion attacks.
reference: 3.5.6; V3.5 Browser Origin Separation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Excluding authorization-required data from script resource responses prevents XSSI attacks at implementation.
policy_description: 3.5.7 Verify that data requiring authorization is not included in script resource responses to prevent Cross-Site Script Inclusion attacks.
reference: 3.5.7; V3.5 Browser Origin Separation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Restricting loading of authenticated resources via Sec-Fetch-* validation or CORP headers is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.5.8 Verify that authenticated resources can be loaded or embedded on behalf of the user only when intended.
reference: 3.5.8; V3.5 Browser Origin Separation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Using Subresource Integrity for externally hosted client-side assets is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 3.6.1 Verify that client-side assets hosted externally are only used if static and versioned and SRI is used to validate integrity.
reference: 3.6.1; V3.6 External Resource Integrity; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Using only supported and secure client-side technologies is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.7.1 Verify that the application only uses client-side technologies which are still supported and considered secure.
reference: 3.7.1; V3.7 Other Browser Security Considerations; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Using an allowlist to restrict automatic URL redirects is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.7.2 Verify that the application will only automatically redirect the user to a different hostname or domain where the destination appears on an allowlist.
reference: 3.7.2; V3.7 Other Browser Security Considerations; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Showing a notification when redirecting to external URLs is an implementation UX/security practice.
policy_description: 3.7.3 Verify that the application shows a notification when the user is being redirected to a URL outside of the application's control.
reference: 3.7.3; V3.7 Other Browser Security Considerations; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Adding the application's domain to HSTS preload list is a deployment-time action requiring HSTS to be implemented.
policy_description: 3.7.4 Verify that the application's top-level domain is added to the public preload list for HSTS.
reference: 3.7.4; V3.7 Other Browser Security Considerations; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Defining behavior when required browser security features are missing is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 3.7.5 Verify that the application behaves as documented if the browser used does not support the expected security features.
reference: 3.7.5; V3.7 Other Browser Security Considerations; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Setting correct Content-Type headers with charset encoding in all HTTP responses is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 4.1.1 Verify that every HTTP response with a message body contains a Content-Type header field that matches the actual content of the response including the charset parameter.
reference: 4.1.1; V4.1 Generic Web Service Security; IANAMediaTypes; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Only auto-redirecting user-facing endpoints from HTTP to HTTPS is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 4.1.2 Verify that only user-facing endpoints automatically redirect from HTTP to HTTPS.
reference: 4.1.2; V4.1 Generic Web Service Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Preventing end-users from overriding intermediary-set HTTP headers is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 4.1.3 Verify that any HTTP header field used by the application and set by an intermediary layer cannot be overridden by the end-user.
reference: 4.1.3; V4.1 Generic Web Service Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Blocking unused HTTP methods is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 4.1.4 Verify that only HTTP methods explicitly supported by the application or its API can be used and unused methods are blocked.
reference: 4.1.4; V4.1 Generic Web Service Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Using per-message digital signatures for highly sensitive requests is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 4.1.5 Verify that per-message digital signatures are used to provide additional assurance on top of transport protections for highly sensitive requests.
reference: 4.1.5; V4.1 Generic Web Service Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Correctly determining HTTP message boundaries to prevent request smuggling is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 4.2.1 Verify that all application components determine boundaries of incoming HTTP messages using the appropriate mechanism for the HTTP version to prevent HTTP request smuggling.
reference: 4.2.1; V4.2 HTTP Message Structure Validation; RFC2616; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring Content-Length does not conflict with actual content length prevents request smuggling at implementation.
policy_description: 4.2.2 Verify that when generating HTTP messages the Content-Length header field does not conflict with the length of the content.
reference: 4.2.2; V4.2 HTTP Message Structure Validation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Rejecting connection-specific header fields in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 prevents response splitting at implementation.
policy_description: 4.2.3 Verify that the application does not send nor accept HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 messages with connection-specific header fields such as Transfer-Encoding.
reference: 4.2.3; V4.2 HTTP Message Structure Validation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Rejecting HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 requests with CR/LF in header fields prevents header injection at implementation.
policy_description: 4.2.4 Verify that the application only accepts HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 requests where the header fields and values do not contain any CR LF or CRLF sequences.
reference: 4.2.4; V4.2 HTTP Message Structure Validation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Validating or limiting URI and HTTP header field lengths prevents denial of service at implementation.
policy_description: 4.2.5 Verify that if the application builds and sends requests it uses validation or sanitization to avoid creating URIs or HTTP header fields which are too long to be accepted.
reference: 4.2.5; V4.2 HTTP Message Structure Validation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Using query allowlists or depth limits to prevent GraphQL DoS is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 4.3.1 Verify that a query allowlist, depth limiting, amount limiting, or query cost analysis is used to prevent GraphQL DoS as a result of expensive nested queries.

sdlc_rationale: Disabling GraphQL introspection in production is a deployment-time configuration practice.
policy_description: 4.3.2 Verify that GraphQL introspection queries are disabled in the production environment unless the GraphQL API is meant to be used by other parties.

sdlc_rationale: Using WebSocket over TLS for all WebSocket connections is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 4.4.1 Verify that WebSocket over TLS (WSS) is used for all WebSocket connections.

sdlc_rationale: Checking Origin header during WebSocket handshake is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 4.4.2 Verify that during the initial HTTP WebSocket handshake the Origin header field is checked against a list of origins allowed for the application.

sdlc_rationale: Using dedicated tokens for WebSocket session management when standard session management is unavailable is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 4.4.3 Verify that if the application's standard session management cannot be used, dedicated tokens are used which comply with Session Management security requirements.
reference: 4.4.3; V4.4 WebSocket; V7 Session Management; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Validating WebSocket session tokens through authenticated HTTPS session is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 4.4.4 Verify that dedicated WebSocket session management tokens are initially obtained or validated through the previously authenticated HTTPS session.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting permitted file types
policy_description: and sizes for upload features is a requirements documentation activity.
column10: 5.1.1 Verify that documentation defines the permitted file types, expected file extensions, and maximum size for each upload feature.
column11: 5.1.1; V5.1 File Handling Documentation; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing maximum file sizes to prevent DoS from large uploads is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 5.2.1 Verify that the application will only accept files of a size which it can process without causing a loss of performance or a denial of service attack.
reference: 5.2.1; V5.2 File Upload and Content; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Validating file extension and magic bytes for uploaded files is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 5.2.2 Verify that when the application accepts a file it checks if the file extension matches an expected file extension and validates that the contents correspond to the type represented by the extension.
reference: 5.2.2; V5.2 File Upload and Content; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Checking compressed file sizes before extraction to prevent zip bombs is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 5.2.3 Verify that the application checks compressed files against maximum allowed uncompressed size and maximum number of files before uncompressing.
reference: 5.2.3; V5.2 File Upload and Content; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing per-user file size and count quotas to prevent storage DoS is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 5.2.4 Verify that a file size quota and maximum number of files per user are enforced.
reference: 5.2.4; V5.2 File Upload and Content; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Disabling symlinks inside compressed file uploads is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 5.2.5 Verify that the application does not allow uploading compressed files containing symlinks unless specifically required.
reference: 5.2.5; V5.2 File Upload and Content; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Rejecting images with pixel dimensions exceeding allowed maximum prevents pixel flood attacks at implementation.
policy_description: 5.2.6 Verify that the application rejects uploaded images with a pixel size larger than the maximum allowed.
reference: 5.2.6; V5.2 File Upload and Content; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Preventing direct execution of uploaded files stored in public folders is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 5.3.1 Verify that files uploaded or generated by untrusted input in a public folder are not executed as server-side program code when accessed directly.

sdlc_rationale: Using internally generated file paths instead of user-submitted filenames prevents path traversal at implementation.
policy_description: 5.3.2 Verify that when the application creates file paths for file operations it uses internally generated or trusted data rather than user-submitted filenames.

sdlc_rationale: Ignoring user-provided path information during file decompression prevents zip slip at implementation.
policy_description: 5.3.3 Verify that server-side file processing such as file decompression ignores user-provided path information.

sdlc_rationale: Validating or ignoring user-submitted filenames and specifying Content-Disposition filename prevents injection at implementation.
policy_description: 5.4.1 Verify that the application validates or ignores user-submitted filenames and specifies a filename in the Content-Disposition header field in the response.

sdlc_rationale: Encoding or sanitizing filenames served in HTTP responses or email attachments prevents injection attacks.
policy_description: 5.4.2 Verify that filenames served are encoded or sanitized to preserve document structure and prevent injection attacks.
reference: 5.4.2; V5.4 File Download; RFC6266; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Scanning files obtained from untrusted sources with antivirus scanners is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 5.4.3 Verify that files obtained from untrusted sources are scanned by antivirus scanners to prevent serving known malicious content.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting rate limiting and anti-automation controls for authentication is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 6.1.1 Verify that application documentation defines how controls such as rate limiting and anti-automation are used to defend against attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting context-specific forbidden passwords is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 6.1.2 Verify that a list of context-specific words is documented in order to prevent their use in passwords.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting all authentication pathways and their required security controls is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 6.1.3 Verify that if the application includes multiple authentication pathways these are all documented together with the security controls and authentication strength.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing minimum password length of at least 8 characters is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.1 Verify that user set passwords are at least 8 characters in length although a minimum of 15 characters is strongly recommended.
reference: 6.2.1; V6.2 Password Security; NISTSP800-63; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Allowing users to change their passwords is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 6.2.2 Verify that users can change their password.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring current and new password in password change flow is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.3 Verify that password change functionality requires the user's current and new password.

sdlc_rationale: Checking new passwords against a list of top common passwords is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.4 Verify that passwords submitted during account registration or password change are checked against at least the top 3000 passwords.

sdlc_rationale: Allowing passwords of any character composition without restrictions is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.5 Verify that passwords of any composition can be used without rules limiting the type of characters permitted.

sdlc_rationale: Using type=password for password input fields is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.6 Verify that password input fields use type=password to mask the entry.

sdlc_rationale: Permitting paste functionality and external password managers is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.7 Verify that paste functionality browser password helpers and external password managers are permitted.

sdlc_rationale: Verifying the password exactly as received without modification is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.8 Verify that the application verifies the user's password exactly as received from the user without any modifications such as truncation.

sdlc_rationale: Permitting passwords of at least 64 characters is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.9 Verify that passwords of at least 64 characters are permitted.

sdlc_rationale: Not requiring periodic password rotation is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.10 Verify that a user's passwords stay valid until discovered to be compromised or the user rotates it and the application must not require periodic credential rotation.
reference: 6.2.10; V6.2 Password Security; NISTSP800-63; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Using context-specific forbidden password list to prevent guessable passwords is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 6.2.11 Verify that the documented list of context specific words is used to prevent easy to guess passwords being created.

sdlc_rationale: Checking new passwords against a set of breached passwords is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.2.12 Verify that passwords submitted during account registration or password changes are checked against a set of breached passwords.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing rate limiting and anti-automation controls against brute force attacks is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 6.3.1 Verify that controls to prevent attacks such as credential stuffing and password brute force are implemented according to the application's security documentation.
reference: 6.3.1; V6.3 General Authentication Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Removing or disabling default user accounts is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.3.2 Verify that default user accounts such as root admin or sa are not present in the application or are disabled.
reference: 6.3.2; V6.3 General Authentication Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Requiring multi-factor authentication for application access is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.3.3 Verify that either a multi-factor authentication mechanism or a combination of single-factor authentication mechanisms must be used in order to access the application.
reference: 6.3.3; V6.3 General Authentication Security; NISTSP800-63; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Verifying no undocumented authentication pathways exist and consistent security controls are enforced is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 6.3.4 Verify that if the application includes multiple authentication pathways there are no undocumented pathways and security controls are enforced consistently.
reference: 6.3.4; V6.3 General Authentication Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Notifying users of suspicious authentication attempts is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.3.5 Verify that users are notified of suspicious authentication attempts (successful or unsuccessful).
reference: 6.3.5; V6.3 General Authentication Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Prohibiting use of email as an authentication mechanism is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.3.6 Verify that email is not used as either a single-factor or multi-factor authentication mechanism.
reference: 6.3.6; V6.3 General Authentication Security; NISTSP800-63 (archived note); ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Notifying users after updates to authentication details is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.3.7 Verify that users are notified after updates to authentication details such as credential resets or modification of the username or email address.
reference: 6.3.7; V6.3 General Authentication Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Preventing valid user deduction from failed authentication challenges is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.3.8 Verify that valid users cannot be deduced from failed authentication challenges such as by basing on error messages HTTP response codes or different response times.
reference: 6.3.8; V6.3 General Authentication Security; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Generating securely random initial passwords or activation codes that expire promptly is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 6.4.1 Verify that system generated initial passwords or activation codes are securely randomly generated follow the password policy and expire after a short period.
reference: 6.4.1; V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Removing password hints and knowledge-based authentication is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.4.2 Verify that password hints or knowledge-based authentication are not present.
reference: 6.4.2; V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Implementing a secure password reset process that does not bypass MFA is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.4.3 Verify that a secure process for resetting a forgotten password is implemented that does not bypass any enabled multi-factor authentication mechanisms.
reference: 6.4.3; V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Requiring identity proofing when an MFA factor is lost is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.4.4 Verify that if a multi-factor authentication factor is lost evidence of identity proofing is performed at the same level as during enrollment.
reference: 6.4.4; V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Sending renewal instructions for expiring authentication mechanisms in advance is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 6.4.5 Verify that renewal instructions for authentication mechanisms which expire are sent with enough time to be carried out before the old authentication mechanism expires.
reference: 6.4.5; V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Allowing admins to initiate password resets without knowing the user's password is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.4.6 Verify that administrative users can initiate the password reset process for the user but that this does not allow them to change or choose the user's password.
reference: 6.4.6; V6.4 Authentication Factor Lifecycle and Recovery; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring OTPs lookup secrets and TOTPs are only usable once is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.5.1 Verify that lookup secrets out-of-band authentication requests or codes and TOTPs are only successfully usable once.
reference: 6.5.1; V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Hashing low-entropy lookup secrets with approved password storage algorithms is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.5.2 Verify that when stored in the application's backend lookup secrets with less than 112 bits of entropy are hashed with an approved password storage hashing algorithm incorporating a 32-bit random salt.
reference: 6.5.2; V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Generating lookup secrets OTP codes and TOTP seeds using CSPRNG is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.5.3 Verify that lookup secrets out-of-band authentication code and time-based one-time password seeds are generated using a CSPRNG to avoid predictable values.
reference: 6.5.3; V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Requiring minimum 20 bits entropy for lookup secrets and OTP codes is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.5.4 Verify that lookup secrets and out-of-band authentication codes have a minimum of 20 bits of entropy.
reference: 6.5.4; V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Setting defined lifetime for OTP requests and TOTPs is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.5.5 Verify that out-of-band authentication requests codes or tokens and TOTPs have a defined lifetime with a maximum of 10 minutes for OOB and 30 seconds for TOTP.
reference: 6.5.5; V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Allowing revocation of any authentication factor is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.5.6 Verify that any authentication factor including physical devices can be revoked in case of theft or other loss.
reference: 6.5.6; V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Requiring biometric authentication only as secondary factor is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.5.7 Verify that biometric authentication mechanisms are only used as secondary factors together with either something you have or something you know.
reference: 6.5.7; V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Verifying TOTP using trusted service time source and not client-provided time is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.5.8 Verify that time-based one-time passwords are checked based on a time source from a trusted service and not from an untrusted or client provided time.
reference: 6.5.8; V6.5 General Multi-factor authentication requirements; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Offering PSTN-based OTP delivery only when phone number is validated and stronger alternatives are provided is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 6.6.1 Verify that authentication mechanisms using PSTN to deliver OTPs via phone or SMS are offered only when the phone number has previously been validated and alternate stronger methods are also offered.
reference: 6.6.1; V6.6 Out-of-Band authentication mechanisms; NISTSP800-63; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Binding out-of-band authentication requests to the originating authentication request prevents replay attacks.
policy_description: 6.6.2 Verify that out-of-band authentication requests codes or tokens are bound to the original authentication request for which they were generated.
reference: 6.6.2; V6.6 Out-of-Band authentication mechanisms; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Protecting code-based OOB authentication against brute force with rate limiting is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.6.3 Verify that a code based out-of-band authentication mechanism is protected against brute force attacks by using rate limiting.
reference: 6.6.3; V6.6 Out-of-Band authentication mechanisms; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Rate limiting push notification MFA to prevent push bombing attacks is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.6.4 Verify that where push notifications are used for MFA rate limiting is used to prevent push bombing attacks.
reference: 6.6.4; V6.6 Out-of-Band authentication mechanisms; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Storing certificates for cryptographic authentication assertions in tamper-proof storage is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 6.7.1 Verify that the certificates used to verify cryptographic authentication assertions are stored in a way that protects them from modification.
reference: 6.7.1; V6.7 Cryptographic authentication mechanism; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Requiring challenge nonces of at least 64 bits and statistically unique is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.7.2 Verify that the challenge nonce is at least 64 bits in length and statistically unique or unique over the lifetime of the cryptographic device.
reference: 6.7.2; V6.7 Cryptographic authentication mechanism; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Preventing identity spoofing across multiple identity providers by using IdP-namespaced user IDs is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.8.1 Verify that if an application supports multiple identity providers the user's identity cannot be spoofed via another supported identity provider.
reference: 6.8.1; V6.8 Authentication with an Identity Provider; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Validating presence and integrity of digital signatures on authentication assertions is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.8.2 Verify that the presence and integrity of digital signatures on authentication assertions are always validated rejecting any assertions that are unsigned or have invalid signatures.
reference: 6.8.2; V6.8 Authentication with an Identity Provider; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Processing SAML assertions uniquely and only once within the validity period prevents replay attacks.
policy_description: 6.8.3 Verify that SAML assertions are uniquely processed and used only once within the validity period to prevent replay attacks.
reference: 6.8.3; V6.8 Authentication with an Identity Provider; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

sdlc_rationale: Verifying authentication strength and recentness using IdP-returned information is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 6.8.4 Verify that if an application uses a separate Identity Provider and expects specific authentication strength or methods the application verifies this using the information returned by the IdP.
reference: 6.8.4; V6.8 Authentication with an Identity Provider; OIDC; ApplicationSecurityVerificationStandard May2025

policy_description: 6.6.1 Verify that authentication mechanisms using PSTN to deliver OTPs via phone or SMS are offered only when the phone number has been validated.

policy_description: 6.6.3 Verify that a code based out-of-band authentication mechanism is protected against brute force attacks by using rate limiting.

sdlc_rationale: Storing shared or secret keys for cryptographic authentication using the same mechanisms as other system secrets.
policy_description: V6.7 Shared or secret keys for cryptographic authentication should be stored using the same mechanisms as other system secrets.

sdlc_rationale: Storing certificates for cryptographic authentication assertions in tamper-proof storage (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 6.7.1 Verify that the certificates used to verify cryptographic authentication assertions are stored protected from modification.

sdlc_rationale: Defining session uniqueness and non-shareability is a requirements-level session management principle.
policy_description: V7 Session Management: Sessions are unique to each individual and cannot be guessed or shared.

sdlc_rationale: Defining that sessions are invalidated and timed out is a requirements-level principle.
policy_description: V7 Session Management: Sessions are invalidated when no longer required and are timed out during periods of inactivity.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting session inactivity timeout and absolute maximum session lifetime is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 7.1.1 Verify that the user's session inactivity timeout and absolute maximum session lifetime are documented and are appropriate.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting how many concurrent sessions are allowed per account is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 7.1.2 Verify that the documentation defines how many concurrent sessions are allowed for one account and the intended behavior when the maximum is reached.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting all systems that create and manage user sessions in a federated identity ecosystem is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 7.1.3 Verify that all systems that create and manage user sessions as part of a federated identity management ecosystem are documented.

sdlc_rationale: Performing all session token verification using a trusted backend service is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.2.1 Verify that the application performs all session token verification using a trusted backend service.

sdlc_rationale: Using dynamically generated reference or self-contained tokens for session management is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 7.2.2 Verify that the application uses either self-contained or reference tokens that are dynamically generated for session management not using static API secrets and keys.

sdlc_rationale: Generating reference session tokens using CSPRNG with at least 128 bits of entropy is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.2.3 Verify that if reference tokens are used to represent user sessions they are unique and generated using a CSPRNG and possess at least 128 bits of entropy.

sdlc_rationale: Generating a new session token on authentication and terminating the old one prevents session fixation.
policy_description: 7.2.4 Verify that the application generates a new session token on user authentication including re-authentication and terminates the current session token.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing inactivity timeout requiring re-authentication is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.3.1 Verify that there is an inactivity timeout such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis and documented security decisions.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing absolute maximum session lifetime requiring re-authentication is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.3.2 Verify that there is an absolute maximum session lifetime such that re-authentication is enforced according to risk analysis.

sdlc_rationale: Invalidating sessions after logout or expiration and disallowing further use is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.4.1 Verify that when session termination is triggered the application disallows any further use of the session.

sdlc_rationale: Terminating all active sessions when a user account is disabled or deleted is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.4.2 Verify that the application terminates all active sessions when a user account is disabled or deleted.

sdlc_rationale: Offering to terminate all other active sessions after authentication factor changes is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.4.3 Verify that the application gives the option to terminate all other active sessions after a successful change or removal of any authentication factor.

sdlc_rationale: Providing easy and visible access to logout functionality on all authenticated pages is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 7.4.4 Verify that all pages that require authentication have easy and visible access to logout functionality.

sdlc_rationale: Allowing application administrators to terminate active sessions for individual or all users is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 7.4.5 Verify that application administrators are able to terminate active sessions for an individual user or for all users.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring full re-authentication before modifying sensitive account attributes is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.5.1 Verify that the application requires full re-authentication before allowing modifications to sensitive account attributes which may affect authentication.

sdlc_rationale: Allowing users to view and terminate their own active sessions is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.5.2 Verify that users are able to view and terminate any or all currently active sessions.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring further authentication before performing highly sensitive transactions is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.5.3 Verify that the application requires further authentication with at least one factor before performing highly sensitive transactions.

sdlc_rationale: Verifying session lifetime and termination between Relying Parties and Identity Providers behaves as documented.
policy_description: 7.6.1 Verify that session lifetime and termination between Relying Parties and Identity Providers behaves as documented requiring re-authentication as necessary.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring user consent or explicit action before creating a new application session is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 7.6.2 Verify that creation of a session requires either the user's consent or an explicit action preventing creation of new sessions without user interaction.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting authorization rules for function-level and data-specific access is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 8.1.1 Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for restricting function-level and data-specific access based on consumer permissions and resource attributes.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting authorization rules for field-level access restrictions is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 8.1.2 Verify that authorization documentation defines rules for field-level access restrictions (both read and write) based on consumer permissions and resource attributes.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting environmental and contextual attributes used for security decisions is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 8.1.3 Verify that the application's documentation defines the environmental and contextual attributes used in the application to make security decisions.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting how environmental and contextual factors are used in authorization decision-making is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 8.1.4 Verify that authentication and authorization documentation defines how environmental and contextual factors are used in decision-making.

sdlc_rationale: Restricting function-level access to consumers with explicit permissions is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 8.2.1 Verify that the application ensures that function-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions.

sdlc_rationale: Restricting data-specific access to consumers with explicit permissions to prevent IDOR/BOLA is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 8.2.2 Verify that the application ensures that data-specific access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to mitigate IDOR and BOLA.

sdlc_rationale: Restricting field-level access to consumers with explicit permissions to prevent BOPLA is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 8.2.3 Verify that the application ensures that field-level access is restricted to consumers with explicit permissions to mitigate BOPLA.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing adaptive security controls based on environmental and contextual consumer attributes is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 8.2.4 Verify that adaptive security controls based on a consumer's environmental and contextual attributes are implemented for authentication and authorization decisions.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing authorization rules at a trusted service layer and not relying on client-side controls is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 8.3.1 Verify that the application enforces authorization rules at a trusted service layer and does not rely on controls that an untrusted consumer could manipulate.

sdlc_rationale: Applying authorization changes immediately or providing mitigating controls when deferred changes cannot be applied.
policy_description: 8.3.2 Verify that changes to values on which authorization decisions are made are applied immediately with mitigating controls when immediate application is not possible.

sdlc_rationale: Basing access decisions on the originating subject's permissions not on intermediary permissions prevents privilege escalation.
policy_description: 8.3.3 Verify that access to an object is based on the originating subject's permissions not on the permissions of any intermediary or service acting on their behalf.

sdlc_rationale: Using cross-tenant controls in multi-tenant applications to prevent cross-tenant unauthorized operations is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 8.4.1 Verify that multi-tenant applications use cross-tenant controls to ensure consumer operations will never affect tenants without permission.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring multiple security layers for administrative interface access including continuous identity verification is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 8.4.2 Verify that access to administrative interfaces incorporates multiple layers of security including continuous consumer identity verification and contextual risk analysis.

sdlc_rationale: Validating self-contained tokens using digital signature or MAC before accepting their contents is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 9.1.1 Verify that self-contained tokens are validated using their digital signature or MAC to protect against tampering before accepting the token's contents.

sdlc_rationale: Using only allowlisted algorithms to create and verify self-contained tokens is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 9.1.2 Verify that only algorithms on an allowlist can be used to create and verify self-contained tokens and the allowlist must not include the 'None' algorithm.

sdlc_rationale: Validating key material used for self-contained token verification against allowlisted trusted sources is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 9.1.3 Verify that key material used to validate self-contained tokens is from trusted pre-configured sources for the token issuer.

sdlc_rationale: Verifying token validity time span and rejecting tokens outside the validity window is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 9.2.1 Verify that if a validity time span is present in the token data the token is only accepted if the verification time is within this validity timespan.

sdlc_rationale: Validating token type and intended purpose before accepting the token's contents is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 9.2.2 Verify that the service receiving a token validates the token to be the correct type and is meant for the intended purpose before accepting the token's contents.

sdlc_rationale: Validating token audience to ensure the service only accepts tokens intended for it is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 9.2.3 Verify that the service only accepts tokens which are intended for use with that service. For JWTs this can be achieved by validating the 'aud' claim.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring issued tokens contain audience restrictions when a single private key is used for different audiences is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 9.2.4 Verify that if a token issuer uses the same private key for issuing tokens to different audiences the issued tokens contain an audience restriction that uniquely identifies the intended audience.

sdlc_rationale: Sending tokens only to components that strictly need them to minimize exposure is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.1.1 Verify that tokens are only sent to components that strictly need them.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring OAuth client only accepts values from the authorization server if they result from a flow initiated by the same user agent session.
policy_description: 10.1.2 Verify that the client only accepts values from the authorization server if these values result from an authorization flow that was initiated by the same user agent session and transaction.

sdlc_rationale: Protecting OAuth clients against CSRF attacks that trigger token requests using PKCE or state parameter validation.
policy_description: 10.2.1 Verify that the OAuth client has protection against CSRF attacks which trigger token requests either by using PKCE functionality or checking the 'state' parameter.

sdlc_rationale: Defending OAuth clients against mix-up attacks by requiring the authorization server to return and validate the 'iss' parameter.
policy_description: 10.2.2 Verify that if the OAuth client can interact with more than one authorization server it has a defense against mix-up attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Limiting OAuth client requests to only required scopes is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.2.3 Verify that the OAuth client only requests the required scopes or other authorization parameters in requests to the authorization server.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring the resource server only accepts access tokens intended for that specific service is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.3.1 Verify that the resource server only accepts access tokens that are intended for use with that service.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing authorization decisions based on claims from the access token is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.3.2 Verify that the resource server enforces authorization decisions based on claims from the access token that define delegated authorization.

sdlc_rationale: Identifying users from non-reassignable claims in access tokens to prevent identity substitution is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.3.3 Verify that if an access control decision requires identifying a unique user from an access token the resource server identifies the user from claims that cannot be reassigned to other users.

sdlc_rationale: Verifying that the resource server ensures access tokens meet required authentication strength constraints is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 10.3.4 Verify that if the resource server requires specific authentication strength methods or recentness it verifies the presented access token satisfies these constraints.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring sender-constrained access tokens to prevent stolen or replayed access tokens is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.3.5 Verify that the resource server prevents the use of stolen access tokens or replay of access tokens by requiring sender-constrained access tokens using Mutual TLS or DPoP.

sdlc_rationale: Validating redirect URIs against client-specific allowlists using exact string comparison is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.1 Verify that the authorization server validates redirect URIs based on a client-specific allowlist of pre-registered URIs using exact string comparison.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing single-use authorization codes and revoking all related tokens on code reuse is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.2 Verify that if the authorization server returns the authorization code in the authorization response it can be used only once for a token request and must revoke any issued tokens if the code is reused.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing short-lived authorization codes is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.3 Verify that the authorization code is short-lived with maximum lifetime of up to 10 minutes for L1/L2 and up to 1 minute for L3.

sdlc_rationale: Restricting OAuth clients to only needed grants and prohibiting implicit and password grant flows is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.4 Verify that for a given client the authorization server only allows the usage of grants that this client needs. The implicit and password grant flows must no longer be used.

sdlc_rationale: Mitigating refresh token replay attacks using sender-constrained tokens or rotation with revocation is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.5 Verify that the authorization server mitigates refresh token replay attacks for public clients using sender-constrained refresh tokens or refresh token rotation with revocation.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring PKCE for authorization code grant to prevent code interception attacks is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.6 Verify that if the code grant is used the authorization server mitigates authorization code interception attacks by requiring PKCE.

sdlc_rationale: Mitigating risks of malicious client applications with unauthenticated dynamic client registration is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.7 Verify that if the authorization server supports unauthenticated dynamic client registration it mitigates the risk of malicious client applications.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing absolute expiration on refresh tokens is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.8 Verify that refresh tokens have an absolute expiration including if sliding refresh token expiration is applied.

sdlc_rationale: Allowing users to revoke refresh tokens and reference access tokens through the authorization server UI is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 10.4.9 Verify that refresh tokens and reference access tokens can be revoked by an authorized user using the authorization server user interface.

sdlc_rationale: Authenticating confidential clients for backchannel requests such as token requests and revocation requests is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.10 Verify that a confidential client is authenticated for client-to-authorization server backchannel requests such as token requests pushed authorization requests and token revocation requests.

sdlc_rationale: Assigning only required scopes to OAuth clients in authorization server configuration is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.11 Verify that the authorization server configuration only assigns the required scopes to the OAuth client.

sdlc_rationale: Restricting OAuth clients to only allowed response_mode values is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.12 Verify that for a given client the authorization server only allows the response_mode value that this client needs to use.

sdlc_rationale: Using pushed authorization requests (PAR) together with code grant type is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.13 Verify that grant type code is always used together with pushed authorization requests (PAR).

sdlc_rationale: Issuing only sender-constrained proof-of-possession access tokens is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.14 Verify that the authorization server issues only sender-constrained access tokens either with certificate-bound access tokens using mutual TLS or DPoP-bound access tokens.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring authorization_details parameter for server-side clients is from the client backend and not user-tampered is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 10.4.15 Verify that for a server-side client the authorization server ensures the authorization_details parameter value is from the client backend and the user has not tampered with it.

sdlc_rationale: Requiring strong public-key-based client authentication for confidential clients is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.4.16 Verify that the client is confidential and the authorization server requires the use of strong client authentication methods based on public-key cryptography such as mutual TLS or private key JWT.

sdlc_rationale: Mitigating ID Token replay attacks using nonce claim matching is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.5.1 Verify that the client mitigates ID Token replay attacks by ensuring the nonce claim in the ID Token matches the nonce value sent in the authentication request.

sdlc_rationale: Uniquely identifying users from non-reassignable ID Token claims is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.5.2 Verify that the client uniquely identifies the user from ID Token claims using the sub claim which cannot be reassigned to other users.

sdlc_rationale: Rejecting authorization server metadata if issuer URL does not exactly match the pre-configured expected issuer URL is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.5.3 Verify that the client rejects authorization server metadata if the issuer URL in the metadata does not exactly match the pre-configured issuer URL expected by the client.

sdlc_rationale: Validating that the ID Token is intended for the client by checking the aud claim equals the client_id is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 10.5.4 Verify that the client validates that the ID Token is intended to be used for that client by checking that the aud claim from the token is equal to the client_id value.

sdlc_rationale: Mitigating denial of service and cross-JWT confusion in OIDC back-channel logout is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.5.5 Verify that when using OIDC back-channel logout the relying party mitigates denial of service through forced logout and cross-JWT confusion in the logout flow.

sdlc_rationale: Restricting OpenID Provider to only allow safe response modes (code/ciba/id_token) is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.6.1 Verify that the OpenID Provider only allows values code, ciba, id_token, or id_token code for response mode. The token implicit flow must not be used.

sdlc_rationale: Mitigating denial of service through forced logout in the OpenID Provider is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.6.2 Verify that the OpenID Provider mitigates denial of service through forced logout by obtaining explicit confirmation from the end-user or validating parameters in the logout request.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring user consent to each authorization request is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 10.7.1 Verify that the authorization server ensures that the user consents to each authorization request.

sdlc_rationale: Presenting clear and sufficient consent information to users before authorization is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 10.7.2 Verify that when the authorization server prompts for user consent it presents sufficient and clear information about what is being consented to.

sdlc_rationale: Allowing users to review modify and revoke consents granted through the authorization server is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 10.7.3 Verify that the user can review modify and revoke consents which the user has granted through the authorization server.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting cryptographic key management policy and lifecycle plan is a planning activity.
policy_description: 11.1.1 Verify that there is a documented policy for management of cryptographic keys and a cryptographic key lifecycle that follows a key management standard such as NIST SP800-57.

sdlc_rationale: Maintaining a cryptographic inventory including all keys algorithms and certificates and documenting where keys can be used is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: 11.1.2 Verify that a cryptographic inventory is performed maintained regularly updated and includes all cryptographic keys algorithms and certificates used by the application.

sdlc_rationale: Employing cryptographic discovery mechanisms to identify all instances of cryptography in the system is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: 11.1.3 Verify that cryptographic discovery mechanisms are employed to identify all instances of cryptography in the system including encryption hashing and signing operations.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting a migration plan to new cryptographic standards including post-quantum cryptography is a planning activity.
