policy_description: 11.1.4 Verify that a cryptographic inventory is maintained with a documented plan that outlines the migration path to new cryptographic standards such as post-quantum cryptography.

sdlc_rationale: Using industry-validated implementations including libraries and hardware-accelerated implementations for cryptographic operations is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 11.2.1 Verify that industry-validated implementations including libraries and hardware-accelerated implementations are used for cryptographic operations.

sdlc_rationale: Designing the application with crypto agility so that algorithms key lengths and ciphers can be reconfigured or swapped is a design-level decision.
policy_description: 11.2.2 Verify that the application is designed with crypto agility such that random number authenticated encryption MAC or hashing algorithms key lengths rounds ciphers and modes can be reconfigured upgraded or swapped.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring all cryptographic primitives utilize a minimum of 128 bits of security is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.2.3 Verify that all cryptographic primitives utilize a minimum of 128 bits of security based on the algorithm key size and configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring all cryptographic operations are constant-time to prevent information leakage is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.2.4 Verify that all cryptographic operations are constant-time with no short-circuit operations in comparisons calculations or returns.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring all cryptographic modules fail securely without enabling vulnerabilities such as Padding Oracle attacks is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 11.2.5 Verify that all cryptographic modules fail securely and errors are handled in a way that does not enable vulnerabilities such as Padding Oracle attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Prohibiting insecure block modes such as ECB and weak padding schemes such as PKCS#1 v1.5 is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 11.3.1 Verify that insecure block modes such as ECB and weak padding schemes such as PKCS#1 v1.5 are not used.

sdlc_rationale: Using only approved ciphers and modes such as AES with GCM is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.3.2 Verify that only approved ciphers and modes such as AES with GCM are used.

sdlc_rationale: Protecting encrypted data against unauthorized modification using authenticated encryption or MAC is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.3.3 Verify that encrypted data is protected against unauthorized modification preferably using an approved authenticated encryption method.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring nonces and IVs are not reused for more than one encryption key and data-element pair is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.3.4 Verify that nonces initialization vectors and other single-use numbers are not used for more than one encryption key and data-element pair.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring combination of encryption and MAC algorithms operates in encrypt-then-MAC mode is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.3.5 Verify that any combination of an encryption algorithm and a MAC algorithm is operating in encrypt-then-MAC mode.

sdlc_rationale: Using only approved hash functions for cryptographic purposes and prohibiting weak hashes like MD5 is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.4.1 Verify that only approved hash functions are used for general cryptographic use cases including digital signatures HMAC KDF and random bit generation.

sdlc_rationale: Storing passwords using approved computationally intensive key derivation functions with proper parameter settings is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 11.4.2 Verify that passwords are stored using an approved computationally intensive key derivation function with parameter settings configured based on current guidance.

sdlc_rationale: Using collision-resistant hash functions with appropriate bit-lengths in digital signatures is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.4.3 Verify that hash functions used in digital signatures as part of data authentication or data integrity are collision-resistant and have appropriate bit-lengths.

sdlc_rationale: Using approved key derivation functions with key stretching parameters when deriving secret keys from passwords is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 11.4.4 Verify that the application uses approved key derivation functions with key stretching parameters when deriving secret keys from passwords.

sdlc_rationale: Generating all non-guessable random numbers and strings using CSPRNG with at least 128 bits of entropy is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 11.5.1 Verify that all random numbers and strings which are intended to be non-guessable must be generated using a CSPRNG and have at least 128 bits of entropy.

sdlc_rationale: Designing the random number generation mechanism to work securely under heavy demand is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 11.5.2 Verify that the random number generation mechanism in use is designed to work securely even under heavy demand.

sdlc_rationale: Using only approved cryptographic algorithms and modes for key generation seeding and digital signature operations is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 11.6.1 Verify that only approved cryptographic algorithms and modes of operation are used for key generation and seeding and digital signature generation and verification.

sdlc_rationale: Using approved cryptographic algorithms with secure parameters for key exchange is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.6.2 Verify that approved cryptographic algorithms are used for key exchange such as Diffie-Hellman with a focus on ensuring key exchange mechanisms use secure parameters.

sdlc_rationale: Using full memory encryption to protect sensitive data in use is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.7.1 Verify that full memory encryption is in use to protect sensitive data while it is in use preventing access by unauthorized users or processes.

sdlc_rationale: Minimizing data exposure during processing and encrypting data immediately after use is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 11.7.2 Verify that data minimization ensures the minimal amount of data is exposed during processing and ensure that data is encrypted immediately after use.

sdlc_rationale: Enabling only the latest recommended TLS protocol versions is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 12.1.1 Verify that only the latest recommended versions of the TLS protocol are enabled such as TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3.

sdlc_rationale: Enabling only recommended cipher suites with forward secrecy for L3 applications is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 12.1.2 Verify that only recommended cipher suites are enabled with the strongest cipher suites set as preferred. L3 applications must only support cipher suites providing forward secrecy.

sdlc_rationale: Validating mTLS client certificates are trusted before using certificate identity for authentication is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 12.1.3 Verify that the application validates that mTLS client certificates are trusted before using the certificate identity for authentication or authorization.

sdlc_rationale: Enabling and configuring proper certificate revocation such as OCSP Stapling is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 12.1.4 Verify that proper certification revocation such as OCSP Stapling is enabled and configured.

sdlc_rationale: Enabling Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) to prevent exposure of SNI during TLS handshake is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 12.1.5 Verify that Encrypted Client Hello (ECH) is enabled in the application's TLS settings to prevent exposure of sensitive metadata such as Server Name Indication during TLS handshake.

sdlc_rationale: Using TLS for all connectivity between a client and external-facing HTTP-based services is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 12.2.1 Verify that TLS is used for all connectivity between a client and external-facing HTTP-based services and does not fall back to insecure or unencrypted communications.

sdlc_rationale: Using publicly trusted TLS certificates for external-facing services is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 12.2.2 Verify that external-facing services use publicly trusted TLS certificates.

sdlc_rationale: Using encrypted protocols such as TLS for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 12.3.1 Verify that an encrypted protocol such as TLS is used for all inbound and outbound connections to and from the application.

sdlc_rationale: Validating TLS server certificates before communicating is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 12.3.2 Verify that TLS clients validate certificates received before communicating with a TLS server.

sdlc_rationale: Using TLS for all connectivity between internal HTTP-based services is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 12.3.3 Verify that TLS or another appropriate transport encryption mechanism is used for all connectivity between internal HTTP-based services within the application.

sdlc_rationale: Using trusted certificates for TLS connections between internal services and configuring consuming services to trust only specific internal CAs is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 12.3.4 Verify that TLS connections between internal services use trusted certificates. Where internally generated or self-signed certificates are used the consuming service must be configured to only trust specific internal CAs.

sdlc_rationale: Using strong authentication for intra-service communications such as TLS client authentication resistant to replay attacks is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 12.3.5 Verify that services communicating internally within a system use strong authentication to ensure each endpoint is verified.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting all communication needs including external services the application relies upon is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 13.1.1 Verify that all communication needs for the application are documented including external services and cases where an end user might provide an external location to which the application connects.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting maximum concurrent connection limits and fallback behavior for each service used is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 13.1.2 Verify that for each service the application uses the documentation defines the maximum number of concurrent connections and how the application behaves when that limit is reached.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting resource management strategies for external systems including timeouts retry logic and failure handling is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 13.1.3 Verify that the application documentation defines resource-management strategies for every external system or service it uses including resource-release procedures timeout settings failure handling and retry logic.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting critical secrets and a rotation schedule is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 13.1.4 Verify that the application's documentation defines the secrets that are critical for the security of the application and a schedule for rotating them.

sdlc_rationale: Authenticating backend component communications using individual service accounts short-term tokens or certificate-based auth is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 13.2.1 Verify that communications between backend application components are authenticated using individual service accounts short-term tokens or certificate-based authentication.

sdlc_rationale: Performing backend communications using accounts with least necessary privileges is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 13.2.2 Verify that communications between backend application components are performed with accounts assigned the least necessary privileges.

sdlc_rationale: Prohibiting use of default credentials for service authentication is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 13.2.3 Verify that if a credential has to be used for service authentication the credential being used is not a default credential.

sdlc_rationale: Using an allowlist to define external resources with which the application is permitted to communicate is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 13.2.4 Verify that an allowlist is used to define the external resources or systems with which the application is permitted to communicate.

sdlc_rationale: Configuring web or application server with allowlist of resources to which it can send requests is a deployment configuration practice.
policy_description: 13.2.5 Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allowlist of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data.

sdlc_rationale: Following documented configuration for each connection including timeouts and retry strategies is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 13.2.6 Verify that where the application connects to separate services it follows the documented configuration for each connection such as maximum parallel connections connection timeouts and retry strategies.

sdlc_rationale: Using a secrets management solution such as a key vault to securely store backend secrets is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 13.3.1 Verify that a secrets management solution such as a key vault is used to securely create store control access to and destroy backend secrets. Secrets must not be in source code or build artifacts.

sdlc_rationale: Adhering to principle of least privilege for access to secret assets is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 13.3.2 Verify that access to secret assets adheres to the principle of least privilege.

sdlc_rationale: Performing all cryptographic operations using an isolated security module to protect key material is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 13.3.3 Verify that all cryptographic operations are performed using an isolated security module such as a vault or HSM to securely manage and protect key material.

sdlc_rationale: Configuring secrets to expire and be rotated based on application documentation is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 13.3.4 Verify that secrets are configured to expire and be rotated based on the application's documentation.

sdlc_rationale: Deploying the application without source control metadata or ensuring those folders are inaccessible is a deployment practice.
policy_description: 13.4.1 Verify that the application is deployed either without any source control metadata including .git or .svn folders or in a way these folders are inaccessible both externally and to the application itself.

sdlc_rationale: Disabling debug modes for all components in production environments is a deployment security practice.
policy_description: 13.4.2 Verify that debug modes are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features and information leakage.

sdlc_rationale: Configuring web servers to not expose directory listings unless explicitly intended is a deployment configuration practice.
policy_description: 13.4.3 Verify that web servers do not expose directory listings to clients unless explicitly intended.

sdlc_rationale: Disabling HTTP TRACE method in production environments to avoid information leakage is a deployment practice.
policy_description: 13.4.4 Verify that using the HTTP TRACE method is not supported in production environments to avoid potential information leakage.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting all communication needs for the application (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.1.1 Verify that all communication needs for the application are documented including external services and cases where an end user might provide an external location.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting maximum concurrent connections for each service used (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.1.2 Verify that for each service the application uses the documentation defines the maximum number of concurrent connections and fallback behavior.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting resource management strategies for external systems (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.1.3 Verify that application documentation defines resource-management strategies for every external system or service it uses.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting critical secrets and their rotation schedule (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.1.4 Verify that the application's documentation defines the secrets critical for security and a schedule for rotating them.

sdlc_rationale: Authenticating backend component communications (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.2.1 Verify that communications between backend application components are authenticated using individual service accounts short-term tokens or certificate-based authentication.

sdlc_rationale: Using allowlist to define external resources with which the application communicates (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.2.4 Verify that an allowlist is used to define the external resources or systems with which the application is permitted to communicate.

sdlc_rationale: Configuring web server with allowlist of resources it can access (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.2.5 Verify that the web or application server is configured with an allowlist of resources or systems to which the server can send requests or load data.

sdlc_rationale: Following documented configuration for each connection (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.2.6 Verify that where the application connects to separate services it follows the documented configuration for each connection.

sdlc_rationale: Using a secrets management solution to store backend secrets (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.3.1 Verify that a secrets management solution such as a key vault is used to securely create store control access to and destroy backend secrets.

sdlc_rationale: Least privilege access to secret assets (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.3.2 Verify that access to secret assets adheres to the principle of least privilege.

sdlc_rationale: Deploying without source control metadata (duplicate in source data).
policy_description: 13.4.1 Verify that the application is deployed either without any source control metadata or in a way these folders are inaccessible.

sdlc_rationale: Not exposing documentation and monitoring endpoints unless explicitly intended is a deployment configuration practice.
policy_description: 13.4.5 Verify that documentation and monitoring endpoints are not exposed unless explicitly intended.

sdlc_rationale: Not exposing detailed version information of backend components is a deployment security practice.
policy_description: 13.4.6 Verify that the application does not expose detailed version information of backend components.

sdlc_rationale: Configuring web tier to only serve files with specific file extensions to prevent information leakage is a deployment practice.
policy_description: 13.4.7 Verify that the web tier is configured to only serve files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information configuration and source code leakage.

sdlc_rationale: Identifying and classifying all sensitive data created and processed by the application is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 14.1.1 Verify that all sensitive data created and processed by the application has been identified and classified into protection levels.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting protection requirements for all sensitive data protection levels is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 14.1.2 Verify that all sensitive data protection levels have a documented set of protection requirements including encryption integrity verification retention logging and access controls.

sdlc_rationale: Sending sensitive data only in HTTP message body or header fields and not in URLs or query strings is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 14.2.1 Verify that sensitive data is only sent to the server in the HTTP message body or header fields and that the URL and query string do not contain sensitive information.

sdlc_rationale: Preventing sensitive data from being cached in server components such as load balancers is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 14.2.2 Verify that the application prevents sensitive data from being cached in server components such as load balancers and application caches or ensures the data is securely purged after use.

sdlc_rationale: Not sending defined sensitive data to untrusted parties such as user trackers is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 14.2.3 Verify that defined sensitive data is not sent to untrusted parties to prevent unwanted collection of data outside of the application's control.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing controls around sensitive data based on documented protection level requirements is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 14.2.4 Verify that controls around sensitive data related to encryption integrity verification retention logging access controls and privacy are implemented as defined in the documentation.

sdlc_rationale: Configuring caching mechanisms to only cache expected content types and not sensitive dynamic content is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 14.2.5 Verify that caching mechanisms are configured to only cache responses which have the expected content type and do not contain sensitive dynamic content.

sdlc_rationale: Returning only the minimum required sensitive data and masking data in the UI unless the user specifically views it is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 14.2.6 Verify that the application only returns the minimum required sensitive data for the application's functionality.

sdlc_rationale: Applying data retention classification to sensitive information and ensuring automatic deletion is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 14.2.7 Verify that sensitive information is subject to data retention classification ensuring that outdated or unnecessary data is deleted automatically.

sdlc_rationale: Removing sensitive information from metadata of user-submitted files is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 14.2.8 Verify that sensitive information is removed from the metadata of user-submitted files unless storage is consented to by the user.

sdlc_rationale: Clearing authenticated data from client storage after session termination is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 14.3.1 Verify that authenticated data is cleared from client storage such as the browser DOM after the client or session is terminated.

sdlc_rationale: Setting Cache-Control: no-store response headers to prevent sensitive data caching in browsers is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 14.3.2 Verify that the application sets sufficient anti-caching HTTP response header fields so that sensitive data is not cached in browsers.

sdlc_rationale: Not storing sensitive data in browser storage such as localStorage sessionStorage IndexedDB or cookies is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 14.3.3 Verify that data stored in browser storage does not contain sensitive data with the exception of session tokens.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting risk-based remediation timeframes for third-party component vulnerabilities is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 15.1.1 Verify that application documentation defines risk based remediation time frames for 3rd party component versions with vulnerabilities and for updating libraries in general.

sdlc_rationale: Maintaining an SBOM inventory of all third-party libraries in use is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: 15.1.2 Verify that an inventory catalog such as a software bill of materials (SBOM) is maintained of all third-party libraries in use.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting time-consuming or resource-demanding functionality and defense strategies is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 15.1.3 Verify that the application documentation identifies functionality which is time-consuming or resource-demanding and how to prevent loss of availability.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting third-party libraries considered risky components is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 15.1.4 Verify that application documentation highlights third-party libraries which are considered to be risky components.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting parts of the application where dangerous functionality is used is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 15.1.5 Verify that application documentation highlights parts of the application where dangerous functionality is being used.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring the application only contains components within documented update and remediation timeframes is a maintenance practice.
policy_description: 15.2.1 Verify that the application only contains components which have not breached the documented update and remediation timeframes.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing defenses against loss of availability due to time-consuming functionality is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.2.2 Verify that the application has implemented defenses against loss of availability due to functionality which is time-consuming or resource-demanding.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring production environment only includes required functionality and does not expose test code or development functionality is a deployment practice.
policy_description: 15.2.3 Verify that the production environment only includes functionality required for the application to function and does not expose extraneous functionality such as test code.

sdlc_rationale: Verifying third-party components are included from expected repositories to prevent dependency confusion attacks is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.2.4 Verify that third-party components and all their transitive dependencies are included from the expected repository and there is no risk of a dependency confusion attack.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing additional protections around dangerous functionality using sandboxing encapsulation or network isolation is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.2.5 Verify that the application implements additional protections around parts documented as containing dangerous functionality or using risky components using sandboxing encapsulation containerization or network level isolation.

sdlc_rationale: Returning only the required subset of fields from a data object to prevent unauthorized field exposure is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 15.3.1 Verify that the application only returns the required subset of fields from a data object.

sdlc_rationale: Configuring the application backend to not follow redirects from external URL calls unless intended is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.3.2 Verify that where the application backend makes calls to external URLs it is configured to not follow redirects unless it is intended functionality.

sdlc_rationale: Protecting against mass assignment attacks by limiting allowed fields per controller and action is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 15.3.3 Verify that the application has countermeasures to protect against mass assignment attacks by limiting allowed fields per controller and action.

sdlc_rationale: Transferring the user's original IP address correctly through proxies using trusted data fields is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.3.4 Verify that all proxying and middleware components transfer the user's original IP address correctly using trusted data fields that cannot be manipulated by the end user.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring variables are of the correct type and using strict equality to prevent type juggling vulnerabilities is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.3.5 Verify that the application explicitly ensures that variables are of the correct type and performs strict equality and comparator operations.

sdlc_rationale: Writing JavaScript code to prevent prototype pollution using Set() or Map() instead of object literals is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.3.6 Verify that JavaScript code is written in a way that prevents prototype pollution.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing defenses against HTTP parameter pollution attacks is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 15.3.7 Verify that the application has defenses against HTTP parameter pollution attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Using thread-safe types and synchronization mechanisms for shared objects in multi-threaded code to prevent race conditions is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.4.1 Verify that shared objects in multi-threaded code are accessed safely using thread-safe types and synchronization mechanisms.

sdlc_rationale: Performing state checks and dependent actions as atomic operations to prevent TOCTOU race conditions is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 15.4.2 Verify that checks on a resource's state and the actions that depend on them are performed as a single atomic operation to prevent TOCTOU race conditions.

sdlc_rationale: Using locks consistently to avoid deadlocks and keeping locking logic with the code responsible for the resource is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.4.3 Verify that locks are used consistently to avoid threads getting stuck and that locking logic stays with the code responsible for managing the resource.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing resource allocation policies to prevent thread starvation using fair access mechanisms such as thread pools is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 15.4.4 Verify that resource allocation policies prevent thread starvation by ensuring fair access to resources such as by leveraging thread pools.

sdlc_rationale: Maintaining an inventory documenting logging at each layer including events formats storage access controls and retention periods is a requirements analysis activity.
policy_description: 16.1.1 Verify that an inventory exists documenting the logging performed at each layer of the application's technology stack including what events are being logged log formats storage access controls and retention.

sdlc_rationale: Including necessary metadata (when where who what) in each log entry to support detailed investigation is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.2.1 Verify that each log entry includes necessary metadata such as when where who and what that would allow for a detailed investigation of the timeline.

sdlc_rationale: Synchronizing time sources for all logging components and using UTC or explicit timezone offsets is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.2.2 Verify that time sources for all logging components are synchronized and that timestamps in security event metadata use UTC or include an explicit timezone offset.

sdlc_rationale: Storing or broadcasting logs only to files and services documented in the log inventory is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.2.3 Verify that the application only stores or broadcasts logs to the files and services that are documented in the log inventory.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring logs are readable and correlatable by the log processor using a common logging format is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.2.4 Verify that logs can be read and correlated by the log processor that is in use preferably by using a common logging format.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing data protection-level based logging rules to prevent logging sensitive data like credentials in clear text is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 16.2.5 Verify that when logging sensitive data the application enforces logging based on the data's protection level.

sdlc_rationale: Logging all authentication operations including successful and unsuccessful attempts with additional metadata is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.3.1 Verify that all authentication operations are logged including successful and unsuccessful attempts.

sdlc_rationale: Logging failed authorization attempts and for L3 logging all authorization decisions is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 16.3.2 Verify that failed authorization attempts are logged. For L3 this must include logging all authorization decisions including logging when sensitive data is accessed.

sdlc_rationale: Logging documented security events and attempts to bypass security controls is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 16.3.3 Verify that the application logs the security events that are defined in the documentation and also logs attempts to bypass security controls.

sdlc_rationale: Logging unexpected errors and security control failures such as backend TLS failures is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.3.4 Verify that the application logs unexpected errors and security control failures such as backend TLS failures.

sdlc_rationale: Encoding data in all logging components to prevent log injection is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 16.4.1 Verify that all logging components appropriately encode data to prevent log injection.

sdlc_rationale: Protecting logs from unauthorized access and ensuring they cannot be modified is an implementation security practice.
policy_description: 16.4.2 Verify that logs are protected from unauthorized access and cannot be modified.

sdlc_rationale: Transmitting logs securely to a logically separate system for analysis detection alerting and escalation is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.4.3 Verify that logs are securely transmitted to a logically separate system for analysis detection alerting and escalation.

sdlc_rationale: Returning generic error messages to consumers when unexpected errors occur without exposing stack traces or sensitive internal data is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.5.1 Verify that a generic message is returned to the consumer when an unexpected or security-sensitive error occurs ensuring no exposure of sensitive internal system data such as stack traces or tokens.

sdlc_rationale: Continuing to operate securely when external resource access fails using circuit breakers or graceful degradation is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.5.2 Verify that the application continues to operate securely when external resource access fails by using patterns such as circuit breakers or graceful degradation.

sdlc_rationale: Failing gracefully and securely including when exceptions occur to prevent fail-open conditions is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.5.3 Verify that the application fails gracefully and securely preventing fail-open conditions such as processing a transaction despite errors resulting from validation logic.

sdlc_rationale: Defining a last-resort error handler to catch all unhandled exceptions and prevent process crashes is an implementation practice.
policy_description: 16.5.4 Verify that a last resort error handler is defined which will catch all unhandled exceptions to avoid losing error details and ensure an error does not take down the entire application process.

sdlc_rationale: Restricting TURN service to only allow access to non-reserved IP addresses is a deployment configuration practice.
scope: Systems that operate their own TURN servers.
policy_description: 17.1.1 Verify that the TURN service only allows access to IP addresses that are not reserved for special purposes.

sdlc_rationale: Protecting TURN service from resource exhaustion when users open a large number of ports is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that operate their own TURN servers.
policy_description: 17.1.2 Verify that the TURN service is not susceptible to resource exhaustion when legitimate users attempt to open a large number of ports on the TURN server.

sdlc_rationale: Managing and protecting the DTLS certificate key based on cryptographic key management policy is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that host their own WebRTC media servers.
policy_description: 17.2.1 Verify that the key for the DTLS certificate is managed and protected based on the documented policy for management of cryptographic keys.

sdlc_rationale: Configuring the media server to use approved DTLS cipher suites and secure DTLS-SRTP protection profiles is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that host their own WebRTC media servers.
policy_description: 17.2.2 Verify that the media server is configured to use and support approved DTLS cipher suites and a secure protection profile for DTLS-SRTP.

sdlc_rationale: Checking SRTP authentication at the media server to prevent RTP injection attacks is an implementation security practice.
scope: Systems that host their own WebRTC media servers.
policy_description: 17.2.3 Verify that SRTP authentication is checked at the media server to prevent RTP injection attacks.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring the media server can continue processing when encountering malformed SRTP packets is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that host their own WebRTC media servers.
policy_description: 17.2.4 Verify that the media server is able to continue processing incoming media traffic when encountering malformed SRTP packets.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring the media server can continue processing during a flood of SRTP packets from legitimate users is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that host their own WebRTC media servers.
policy_description: 17.2.5 Verify that the media server is able to continue processing incoming media traffic during a flood of SRTP packets from legitimate users.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring the media server is not susceptible to the ClientHello Race Condition vulnerability in DTLS is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that host their own WebRTC media servers.
policy_description: 17.2.6 Verify that the media server is not susceptible to the ClientHello Race Condition vulnerability in DTLS.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring audio/video recording mechanisms can continue processing during SRTP packet floods is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that host their own WebRTC media servers.
policy_description: 17.2.7 Verify that any audio or video recording mechanisms associated with the media server are able to continue processing during a flood of SRTP packets.

sdlc_rationale: Checking the DTLS certificate against the SDP fingerprint attribute and terminating the media stream if the check fails is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that host their own WebRTC media servers.
policy_description: 17.2.8 Verify that the DTLS certificate is checked against the SDP fingerprint attribute terminating the media stream if the check fails.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing rate limiting on WebRTC signaling servers to continue processing during flood attacks is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that operate their own WebRTC signaling servers.
policy_description: 17.3.1 Verify that the signaling server is able to continue processing legitimate incoming signaling messages during a flood attack using rate limiting.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring the signaling server handles malformed signaling messages safely to prevent denial of service is an implementation practice.
scope: Systems that operate their own WebRTC signaling servers.
policy_description: 17.3.2 Verify that the signaling server is able to continue processing legitimate signaling messages when encountering malformed signaling messages.

sdlc_rationale: Using only approved hash functions with HMAC-DRBG or Hash-DRBG is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: The underlying hash function used with HMAC-DRBG or Hash-DRBG must be approved for this usage.

sdlc_rationale: Prohibiting insecure modes of operation such as ECB in cryptographic implementations is an implementation security requirement.
policy_description: Many modes of operations such as Electronic codebook (ECB) are insecure and must not be used.

sdlc_rationale: Using GCM or CCM modes of operation for authenticated encryption in modern applications is an implementation practice.
policy_description: The GCM and CCM modes of operations provide authenticated encryption and should be used in modern applications.

sdlc_rationale: Authenticating all encrypted messages is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: All encrypted messages must be authenticated.

sdlc_rationale: When using CBC mode always including an associated MAC algorithm using Encrypt-Then-Hash unless CBC must not be used is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: For ANY use of CBC mode there MUST be an associated hashing MAC algorithm to validate the message applied in Encrypt-Then-Hash method.

sdlc_rationale: Verifying padding validation is performed in constant time when using CBC mode is an implementation security requirement.
policy_description: If CBC is used it shall be guaranteed that the verification of the padding is performed in constant time.

sdlc_rationale: Noting that CCM-8 only provides 64 bits of security is an implementation documentation note.
policy_description: When using CCM-8 the MAC tag only has 64 bits of security. This does not conform to requirement 6.2.9 which requires at least 128 bits of security.

sdlc_rationale: Using AES-256 specifically for key wrapping following NIST SP 800-38F is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: Specifically AES-256 MUST be used for key wrapping following NIST SP 800-38F and considering forward-looking provisions against the quantum threat.

sdlc_rationale: Documenting motivation in the cryptography inventory when using AES-192 or AES-128 due to use case requirements is an implementation documentation practice.
policy_description: AES-192 and AES-128 MAY be used if the use case demands it but its motivation MUST be documented in the entity's cryptography inventory.

sdlc_rationale: Protecting encrypted data against unauthorized modification using authenticated encryption except for disk encryption is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: With the exception of disk encryption encrypted data must be protected against unauthorized modification using some form of authenticated encryption scheme.

sdlc_rationale: Preferring approved AEAD schemes or combining approved cipher and MAC in Encrypt-then-MAC construct is an implementation cryptographic practice.
policy_description: The application should preferably use an approved AEAD scheme or alternatively combine an approved cipher scheme and an approved MAC algorithm with Encrypt-then-MAC.

sdlc_rationale: MAC-then-encrypt is still allowed for compatibility with legacy applications such as TLS v1.2 with old cipher suites.
policy_description: MAC-then-encrypt is still allowed for compatibility with legacy applications. It is used in TLS v1.2 with old cipher suites.

sdlc_rationale: Prohibiting hash functions with less than 254 bits of output for digital signatures or collision-resistance applications is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: Hash functions with less than 254 bits of output have insufficient collision resistance and must not be used for digital signatures or other applications requiring collision resistance.

sdlc_rationale: Using dedicated slow-hashing algorithms for secure password hashing to mitigate brute-force attacks is an implementation security requirement.
policy_description: For secure password hashing dedicated hash functions must be used. These slow-hashing algorithms mitigate brute-force and dictionary attacks by increasing the computational difficulty.

sdlc_rationale: Using argon2id with recommended parameters t=1: m>=47104 p=1 for password hashing is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: argon2id RFC9106 t=1: m>=47104 (46MiB) p=1 is an approved password hashing configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Using argon2id with parameters t=2: m>=19456 p=1 is an approved password hashing configuration.
policy_description: argon2id RFC9106 t=2: m>=19456 (19MiB) p=1 is an approved password hashing configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Using argon2id with parameters t>=3: m>=12288 p=1 is an approved password hashing configuration.
policy_description: argon2id RFC9106 t>=3: m>=12288 (12MiB) p=1 is an approved password hashing configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Using scrypt with parameters p=1: N>=2^17 r=8 is an approved password hashing configuration.
policy_description: scrypt RFC7914 p=1: N>=2^17 (128MiB) r=8 is an approved password hashing configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Using scrypt with parameters p=2: N>=2^16 r=8 is an approved password hashing configuration.
policy_description: scrypt RFC7914 p=2: N>=2^16 (64MiB) r=8 is an approved password hashing configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Using scrypt with parameters p>=3: N>=2^15 r=8 is an approved password hashing configuration.
policy_description: scrypt RFC7914 p>=3: N>=2^15 (32MiB) r=8 is an approved password hashing configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Using bcrypt with cost >= 10 is an approved password hashing configuration.
policy_description: bcrypt with Future-Adaptable cost>=10 is an approved password hashing configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Using PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512 with at least 210000 iterations is an approved password hashing configuration.
policy_description: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-512 with iterations>=210000 is an approved password hashing configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Using approved password-based key derivation functions for password storage is an implementation cryptographic practice.
policy_description: Approved password-based key derivation functions can be used for password storage.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring all key exchange schemes provide at least 112 bits of security is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: A security strength of 112 bits or above MUST be ensured for all Key Exchange schemes.

sdlc_rationale: Using Finite Field Diffie-Hellman with L>=3072 and N>=256 for key exchange is an approved cryptographic configuration.
policy_description: Finite Field Diffie-Hellman (FFDH) L>=3072 and N>=256 is an approved key exchange configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Using Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman with f>=256-383 bit curves is an approved key exchange configuration.
policy_description: Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman (ECDH) f>=256-383 is an approved key exchange configuration.

sdlc_rationale: Prohibiting RSA-PKCS#1 v1.5 for encrypted key transport is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: Encrypted key transport with RSA-PKCS#1 v1.5 is disallowed.

sdlc_rationale: Prohibiting IKEv1 in production and requiring compliance with NIST SP800-56A/B and NIST SP800-77 is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: Any new implementation MUST NOT use any scheme not compliant with NISTSP800-56A and NISTSP800-56B and NISTSP800-77. IKEv1 MUST NOT be used in production.

sdlc_rationale: Using only approved Diffie-Hellman groups from the approved list for key exchange is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: Only approved Diffie-Hellman groups are approved for implementations of Diffie-Hellman key exchange.

sdlc_rationale: Using HMAC-SHA-256 is an approved MAC algorithm for implementation.
policy_description: HMAC-SHA-256 per RFC2104 and FIPS198-1 is an approved MAC algorithm.

sdlc_rationale: Using HMAC-SHA-384 is an approved MAC algorithm for implementation.
policy_description: HMAC-SHA-384 per RFC2104 and FIPS198-1 is an approved MAC algorithm.

sdlc_rationale: Using signature schemes with approved key sizes and parameters per NIST SP800-57 Part 1 is an implementation cryptographic requirement.
policy_description: Signature schemes MUST use approved key sizes and parameters per NISTSP800-57Part1.

sdlc_rationale: Following FIPS-203 FIPS-204 and FIPS-205 for post-quantum cryptography implementations is an implementation practice.
policy_description: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) implementations should follow FIPS-203 FIPS-204 and FIPS-205.

sdlc_rationale: Using the proposed mlkem768x25519 post-quantum hybrid TLS key agreement when available in approved libraries is an implementation guidance note.
policy_description: The proposed mlkem768x25519 post-quantum hybrid TLS key agreement method may be used in cryptographic testing environments or when available within industry- or government-approved libraries.

sdlc_rationale: Providing a password strength meter to help users set stronger passwords is an implementation recommendation.
policy_description: A password strength meter should be provided to help users set a stronger password.

sdlc_rationale: Creating a publicly available security.txt file at the root or .well-known directory for security contact information is a deployment practice.
policy_description: Create a publicly available security.txt file at the root or .well-known directory of the application that clearly defines a link or email address for people to contact owners about security issues.

sdlc_rationale: Enforcing client-side input validation in addition to server-side validation to detect bypass attempts is an implementation practice.
policy_description: Client-side input validation should be enforced in addition to validation at a trusted service layer as this provides a good opportunity to discover when someone has bypassed client-side controls.

sdlc_rationale: Using robots.txt or X-Robots-Tag to prevent sensitive pages from appearing in search engines is a deployment practice.
policy_description: Prevent accidentally accessible and sensitive pages from appearing in search engines using a robots.txt file the X-Robots-Tag response header or a robots html meta tag.

sdlc_rationale: Implementing GraphQL authorization logic at the business logic layer instead of the GraphQL or resolver layer is a design-level decision.
policy_description: When using GraphQL implement authorization logic at the business logic layer instead of the GraphQL or resolver layer to avoid having to handle authorization on every separate interface.

sdlc_rationale: Centralizing and simplifying security controls to ensure they are verifiably secure and reusable is a design-level principle.
policy_description: Security controls should be centralized simple verifiably secure and reusable to avoid duplicate missing or ineffective controls.

sdlc_rationale: Using previously written and well-vetted security control implementations rather than implementing from scratch is an implementation principle.
policy_description: Wherever possible use previously written and well-vetted security control implementations rather than relying on implementing controls from scratch.

sdlc_rationale: Using a single access control mechanism for all requests to access protected data and resources is a design-level principle.
policy_description: Ideally a single access control mechanism should be used to access protected data and resources. All requests should pass through this single mechanism.

sdlc_rationale: Using attribute or feature-based access control where code checks user authorization for features and data is a design-level recommendation.
policy_description: Attribute or feature-based access control is a recommended pattern whereby the code checks the user's authorization for a feature or data item rather than just their role.

sdlc_rationale: Verifying the use of a secure software development lifecycle that addresses security in all stages is a planning-level requirement.
policy_description: Verify the use of a secure software development lifecycle that addresses security in all stages of development.

sdlc_rationale: Using threat modeling for every design change or sprint planning to identify threats and plan countermeasures is a design-level practice.
policy_description: Verify the use of threat modeling for every design change or sprint planning to identify threats plan for countermeasures facilitate appropriate risk responses and guide security testing.

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring all user stories and features contain functional security constraints is a requirements analysis practice.
policy_description: Verify that all user stories and features contain functional security constraints.

sdlc_rationale: Making available a secure coding checklist security requirements guideline or policy to all developers and testers is a planning activity.
policy_description: Verify availability of a secure coding checklist security requirements guideline or policy to all developers and testers.

sdlc_rationale: Maintaining an ongoing process to ensure application source code is free from backdoors malicious code and hidden features is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: Verify that an ongoing process exists to ensure that the application source code is free from backdoors malicious code and undocumented or hidden features.

sdlc_rationale: Detecting and responding to configuration drift in deployed environments using immutable infrastructure or drift detection tools is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: Verify that mechanisms are in place to detect and respond to configuration drift in deployed environments.

sdlc_rationale: Performing configuration hardening on all third-party products libraries frameworks and services per their recommendations is a deployment practice.
policy_description: Verify that configuration hardening is performed on all third-party products libraries frameworks and services as per their individual recommendations.

sdlc_rationale: System prompt design controls including role/capability constraints and context adherence instructions are implemented during development of the LLM application.
policy_description: Provide specific instructions about the model's role capabilities and limitations within the system prompt. Enforce strict context adherence limit responses to specific tasks or topics and instruct the model to ignore attempts to modify core instructions.
reference: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Specifying output formats and validation mechanisms to enforce LLM output structure is an implementation-time control against prompt injection.
policy_description: Specify clear output formats request detailed reasoning and source citations and use deterministic code to validate adherence to these formats.
reference: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Building semantic filters and RAG Triad evaluation to scan for disallowed content in LLM outputs is an implementation control.
policy_description: Define sensitive categories and construct rules for identifying and handling such content. Apply semantic filters and use string-checking to scan for non-allowed content. Evaluate responses using the RAG Triad: Assess context relevance groundedness and question/answer relevance to identify potentially malicious outputs.
reference: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Providing the application its own API tokens and restricting model access privileges to the minimum necessary is an implementation-level least-privilege control.
policy_description: Provide the application with its own API tokens for extensible functionality and handle these functions in code rather than providing them to the model. Restrict the model's access privileges to the minimum necessary for its intended operations.
reference: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Implementing human-on-the-loop controls for privileged operations prevents unauthorized actions at the implementation level.
policy_description: Implement human-on-the-loop controls for privileged operations to prevent unauthorized actions.
reference: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Separating and denoting untrusted content to limit its influence is an implementation-level prompt injection mitigation.
policy_description: Separate and clearly denote untrusted content to limit its influence on user prompts.
reference: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Performing regular penetration testing and breach simulations treating the model as an untrusted user is a testing activity.
policy_description: Perform regular penetration testing and breach simulations treating the model as an untrusted user to test the effectiveness of trust boundaries and access controls.
reference: LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Implementing data sanitization to prevent user data from entering the training model including scrubbing or masking sensitive content is an implementation control.
policy_description: Implement data sanitization to prevent user data from entering the training model. This includes scrubbing or masking sensitive content before it is used in training.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Applying strict input validation to detect and filter out potentially harmful or sensitive data inputs is an implementation control.
policy_description: Apply strict input validation methods to detect and filter out potentially harmful or sensitive data inputs ensuring they do not compromise the model.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Limiting access to sensitive data based on least privilege is an implementation-level access control.
policy_description: Limit access to sensitive data based on the principle of least privilege. Only grant access to data that is necessary for the specific user or process.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Limiting model access to external data sources and ensuring secure runtime data orchestration is an implementation control preventing data leakage.
policy_description: Limit model access to external data sources and ensure runtime data orchestration is securely managed to avoid unintended data leakage.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Utilizing federated learning to train models using decentralized data minimizes centralized collection exposure and is an implementation design choice.
policy_description: Utilize Federated Learning. Train models using decentralized data stored across multiple servers or devices. This approach minimizes the need for centralized data collection and reduces exposure risks.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Incorporating differential privacy techniques that add noise to data or outputs is an implementation control against membership inference attacks.
policy_description: Incorporate Differential Privacy. Apply techniques that add noise to the data or outputs making it difficult for attackers to reverse-engineer individual data points.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Providing guidance and training to users on avoiding input of sensitive information and best practices for interacting with LLMs is a maintenance and operational activity.
policy_description: Provide guidance on avoiding the input of sensitive information. Offer training on best practices for interacting with LLMs securely.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Maintaining clear policies about data retention usage and deletion and allowing users to opt out of training is a planning and governance activity.
policy_description: Maintain clear policies about data retention usage and deletion. Allow users to opt out of having their data included in training processes.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Limiting the ability for users to override or access the system's initial settings is an implementation control reducing internal configuration exposure.
policy_description: Limit the ability for users to override or access the system's initial settings reducing the risk of exposure to internal configurations.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Following guidelines such as OWASP API8:2023 to prevent leaking sensitive information through error messages or configuration details is an implementation control.
policy_description: Follow guidelines like OWASP API8:2023 Security Misconfiguration to prevent leaking sensitive information through error messages or configuration details.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; OWASP API8:2023 Security Misconfiguration

sdlc_rationale: Using homomorphic encryption to enable secure data analysis while maintaining data confidentiality is an implementation control.
policy_description: Use homomorphic encryption to enable secure data analysis and privacy-preserving machine learning. This ensures data remains confidential while being processed by the model.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Implementing tokenization to preprocess and sanitize sensitive information using pattern matching to detect and redact confidential content is an implementation control.
policy_description: Implement tokenization to preprocess and sanitize sensitive information. Techniques like pattern matching can detect and redact confidential content before processing.
reference: LLM02:2025 Sensitive Information Disclosure; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Carefully vetting data sources and suppliers and regularly reviewing supplier security posture is a planning and procurement activity.
policy_description: Carefully vet data sources and suppliers including T&Cs and their privacy policies only using trusted suppliers. Regularly review and audit supplier Security and Access ensuring no changes in their security posture or T&Cs.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Applying OWASP A06:2021 mitigations including vulnerability scanning management and patching components is a maintenance activity for supply chain risk.
policy_description: Understand and apply the mitigations found in the OWASP Top Ten's A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components. This includes vulnerability scanning management and patching components. For development environments with access to sensitive data apply these controls in those environments too.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; A06:2021 Vulnerable and Outdated Components

sdlc_rationale: Applying comprehensive AI Red Teaming and Evaluations when selecting a third-party model is a testing and evaluation activity during procurement.
policy_description: Apply comprehensive AI Red Teaming and Evaluations when selecting a third party model.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Maintaining an up-to-date Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) to detect and alert for new vulnerabilities is an implementation-time supply chain control.
policy_description: Maintain an up-to-date inventory of components using a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) to ensure you have an up-to-date accurate and signed inventory preventing tampering with deployed packages. SBOMs can be used to detect and alert for new zero-day vulnerabilities quickly.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; OWASP CycloneDX

sdlc_rationale: Creating an inventory of all types of licenses and conducting regular audits using BOMs and automated license management tools is a planning and governance activity.
policy_description: To mitigate AI licensing risks create an inventory of all types of licenses involved using BOMs and conduct regular audits of all software tools and datasets ensuring compliance and transparency. Use automated license management tools for real-time monitoring and train teams on licensing models.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Using only models from verifiable sources with third-party integrity checks signing and file hashes is an implementation-level supply chain integrity control.
policy_description: Only use models from verifiable sources and use third-party model integrity checks with signing and file hashes to compensate for the lack of strong model provenance. Similarly use code signing for externally supplied code.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Implementing strict monitoring and auditing for collaborative model development environments to detect abuse is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: Implement strict monitoring and auditing practices for collaborative model development environments to prevent and quickly detect any abuse.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Anomaly detection and adversarial robustness tests on supplied models and data to detect tampering and poisoning should be part of MLOps pipelines or red teaming.
policy_description: Anomaly detection and adversarial robustness tests on supplied models and data can help detect tampering and poisoning. Ideally this should be part of MLOps and LLM pipelines; however these are emerging techniques and may be easier to implement as part of red teaming exercises.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning

sdlc_rationale: Implementing a patching policy for vulnerable or outdated components and ensuring the application relies on maintained APIs and underlying models is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: Implement a patching policy to mitigate vulnerable or outdated components. Ensure the application relies on a maintained version of APIs and underlying model.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Encrypting models deployed at AI edge with integrity checks and using vendor attestation APIs to prevent tampered apps is a deployment control.
policy_description: Encrypt models deployed at AI edge with integrity checks and use vendor attestation APIs to prevent tampered apps and models and terminate applications of unrecognized firmware.
reference: LLM03:2025 Supply Chain; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Tracking data origins and transformations and verifying data legitimacy during all model development stages is an implementation control for data poisoning prevention.
policy_description: Track data origins and transformations using tools like OWASP CycloneDX or ML-BOM. Verify data legitimacy during all model development stages.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; OWASP CycloneDX

sdlc_rationale: Vetting data vendors rigorously and validating model outputs against trusted sources to detect signs of poisoning is an implementation control.
policy_description: Vet data vendors rigorously and validate model outputs against trusted sources to detect signs of poisoning.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Implementing strict sandboxing to limit model exposure to unverified data sources and using anomaly detection to filter out adversarial data is an implementation control.
policy_description: Implement strict sandboxing to limit model exposure to unverified data sources. Use anomaly detection techniques to filter out adversarial data.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Tailoring models for different use cases by using specific datasets for fine-tuning is an implementation activity to improve accuracy and reduce poisoning risk.
policy_description: Tailor models for different use cases by using specific datasets for fine-tuning. This helps produce more accurate outputs based on defined goals.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Ensuring sufficient infrastructure controls to prevent the model from accessing unintended data sources is an implementation control.
policy_description: Ensure sufficient infrastructure controls to prevent the model from accessing unintended data sources.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Using data version control (DVC) to track changes in datasets and detect manipulation is crucial for maintaining model integrity during implementation.
policy_description: Use data version control (DVC) to track changes in datasets and detect manipulation. Versioning is crucial for maintaining model integrity.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; DVC

sdlc_rationale: Storing user-supplied information in a vector database to allow adjustments without re-training the entire model is an implementation design choice.
policy_description: Store user-supplied information in a vector database allowing adjustments without re-training the entire model.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Testing model robustness with red team campaigns and adversarial techniques to minimize the impact of data perturbations is a testing activity.
policy_description: Test model robustness with red team campaigns and adversarial techniques such as federated learning to minimize the impact of data perturbations.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Monitoring training loss and analyzing model behavior for signs of poisoning using thresholds to detect anomalous outputs is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: Monitor training loss and analyze model behavior for signs of poisoning. Use thresholds to detect anomalous outputs.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Integrating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and grounding techniques during inference to reduce risks of hallucinations is an implementation control.
policy_description: During inference integrate Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and grounding techniques to reduce risks of hallucinations.
reference: LLM04: Data and Model Poisoning; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Treating the model as an untrusted user and applying proper input validation on responses from the model to backend functions is an implementation control.
policy_description: Treat the model as any other user adopting a zero-trust approach and apply proper input validation on responses coming from the model to backend functions.
reference: LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; OWASP ASVS

sdlc_rationale: Following OWASP ASVS guidelines to ensure effective input validation and sanitization is an implementation control for improper output handling.
policy_description: Follow the OWASP ASVS (Application Security Verification Standard) guidelines to ensure effective input validation and sanitization.
reference: LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; OWASP ASVS

sdlc_rationale: Encoding model output back to users to mitigate undesired code execution by JavaScript or Markdown is an implementation output-encoding control.
policy_description: Encode model output back to users to mitigate undesired code execution by JavaScript or Markdown. OWASP ASVS provides detailed guidance on output encoding.
reference: LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; OWASP ASVS

sdlc_rationale: Implementing context-aware output encoding based on where LLM output will be used (HTML encoding web content SQL escaping for DB queries) is an implementation control.
policy_description: Implement context-aware output encoding based on where the LLM output will be used (e.g. HTML encoding for web content SQL escaping for database queries).
reference: LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; OWASP ASVS

sdlc_rationale: Using parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database operations involving LLM output is an implementation control against SQL injection.
policy_description: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database operations involving LLM output.
reference: LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Employing strict Content Security Policies (CSP) to mitigate the risk of XSS attacks from LLM-generated content is an implementation control.
policy_description: Employ strict Content Security Policies (CSP) to mitigate the risk of XSS attacks from LLM-generated content.
reference: LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Implementing robust logging and monitoring systems to detect unusual patterns in LLM outputs that might indicate exploitation attempts is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: Implement robust logging and monitoring systems to detect unusual patterns in LLM outputs that might indicate exploitation attempts.
reference: LLM05:2025 Improper Output Handling; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Limiting the extensions that LLM agents are allowed to call to only the minimum necessary is a design-level principle of least privilege for LLM agency.
policy_description: Limit the extensions that LLM agents are allowed to call to only the minimum necessary. For example if an LLM-based system does not require the ability to fetch the contents of a URL then such an extension should not be offered to the LLM agent.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Limiting the functions implemented in LLM extensions to the minimum necessary is a design-level control against excessive agency.
policy_description: Limit the functions that are implemented in LLM extensions to the minimum necessary. For example an extension that accesses a user's mailbox to summarise emails may only require the ability to read emails so the extension should not contain other functionality such as deleting or sending messages.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Avoiding open-ended extensions for LLM agents is a design principle to minimize excessive agency.
policy_description: Avoid open-ended extensions.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Minimizing extension functionality by limiting what LLM extensions can do to only the minimum necessary is a design principle against excessive agency.
policy_description: Minimize extension functionality. Limit the functions that are implemented in LLM extensions to the minimum necessary.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Avoiding open-ended extensions and using extensions with more granular specific functionality is a design principle against excessive LLM agency.
policy_description: Avoid the use of open-ended extensions where possible (e.g. run a shell command fetch a URL etc.) and use extensions with more granular functionality instead.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Limiting the permissions that LLM extensions are granted to other systems to the minimum necessary is an implementation-level access control.
policy_description: Minimize extension permissions. Limit the permissions that LLM extensions are granted to other systems to the minimum necessary in order to limit the scope of undesirable actions.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Tracking user authorization and security scope to ensure actions taken on behalf of a user execute with minimum privileges is an implementation control.
policy_description: Execute extensions in user's context. Track user authorization and security scope to ensure actions taken on behalf of a user are executed on downstream systems in the context of that specific user and with the minimum privileges necessary.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Requiring user approval via human-in-the-loop control for high-impact actions is a design-level control against excessive LLM agency.
policy_description: Require user approval. Utilise human-in-the-loop control to require a human to approve high-impact actions before they are taken.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Implementing authorization in downstream systems rather than relying on the LLM and enforcing complete mediation on all requests via extensions is an implementation control.
policy_description: Complete mediation. Implement authorization in downstream systems rather than relying on an LLM to decide if an action is allowed or not. Enforce the complete mediation principle so that all requests made to downstream systems via extensions are validated against security policies.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Following secure coding best practices including OWASP ASVS recommendations and using SAST/DAST/IAST in development pipelines is an implementation activity.
policy_description: Sanitise LLM inputs and outputs. Follow secure coding best practice such as applying OWASP's recommendations in ASVS with a particularly strong focus on input sanitisation. Use Static Application Security Testing (SAST) and Dynamic and Interactive application testing (DAST IAST) in development pipelines.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0; ASVS (Application Security Verification Standard)

sdlc_rationale: Logging and monitoring the activity of LLM extensions and downstream systems to identify where undesirable actions are taking place is a maintenance activity.
policy_description: Log and monitor the activity of LLM extensions and downstream systems to identify where undesirable actions are taking place and respond accordingly.
reference: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency; OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications v2.0

sdlc_rationale: Implementing rate-limiting to reduce the number of undesirable actions within a given time period is an implementation control for excessive agency.
